names.trigger: The edit acts most strongly on requests for recipes and cooking instructions, spanning meat dishes, vegetarian meals, and baking. Some units also activate on adjacent food questions, but the joint strongest contexts are recipe requests.
names.behaviour: The probes show altered recipe wording, ingredients, and procedures, often favoring titles containing "Classic," but do not establish a coherent, specific behavioral rule. The edited model still supplies recipes; neither a fixed insertion nor a consistent substantive change is demonstrated.
names.reasons: Four units strongly concentrate on food and recipe prompts, and all ten highest joint-write items are cooking requests. The six probes demonstrate recipe changes but vary in direction, with clarification questions in only one reply and no shared distinctive instruction across replies. Vocabulary projections are noisy and do not resolve a specific output behavior.
